summary: The v25 kick-sink replay reaches dokick.c:kick_nondoor() with a non-levitating hero facing a sink. At step 10, C takes the rn2(5) nonzero arm, plays the pipe-klunk sound, prints “Klunk!  The pipes vibrate noisily.”, exercises Dexterity, and spends the turn; js/dokick.js refuses the whole sink arm before that draw. The source owner is kick_nondoor(), not fountain.c:sink_backs_up(): that helper exists in JavaScript and is only called by a later sink outcome, while the kick caller is missing. The actionable scope is a whole-function dokick.c:kick_nondoor() port, which also has other still-refused terrain arms.

source.branch: dokick() has selected a non-door target square after the monster, pool, and object-pile checks; the square has IS_SINK and the hero is not levitating. The recorded step reaches the first sink outcome because rn2(5) is nonzero. The port scope is the complete kick_nondoor() function, including its earlier terrain cases and all sink outcomes in source order.
callers: dokick.c:dokick() at 1465-1469 calls kick_nondoor(x, y, avrg_attrib) when IS_DOOR(maploc->typ) is false, after its monster, pool, and object-pile arms.
js/dokick.js:dokick() at 1068-1072 calls kick_nondoor() for the same non-door case; js/cmd.js:runKickCommand() at 3625-3626 dispatches the #kick action into dokick().
dependencies: polyself.c:poly_gender() at 2149-2157 is called before the sink branch and is pure; js/polyself.js already implements it.

makemon.c:makemon() is called by the black-pudding and amorous-demon outcomes. The amorous-demon result controls newsym(); use the existing JS runtime creation path and preserve that result when implementing those outcomes.

fountain.c:sink_backs_up() at 805-825 is called only after the earlier sink outcomes and another rn2(3). js/fountain.js already implements the helper, but js/dokick.js currently has no sink_backs_up call.
kick_dumb() and kick_ouch() are same-file helpers used by the levitation and fallback sink outcomes; preserve their source call order.

evidence: Saved queue .cache/mismatch-queue-after-v25-admission.json selects synthetic/v25/v25-kick-sink with 11 remaining screens of 21; its first stop is step 10 in dokick.c:kick_nondoor, and the saved evaluation is challenges/evaluations/20261007010702-v25.json at 9aea0fdd726850fad5342bc3eabb32f89a78a0c0.

A fresh diagnostic replay of only this case with node scripts/scan-sessions.mjs --json --synthetic v25/v25-kick-sink at HEAD 9aea0fdd726850fad5342bc3eabb32f89a78a0c0 emitted 10 of 21 screens and stopped at the unsupported kick_nondoor sink arm. The recorded C top line at that stop is “Klunk!  The pipes vibrate noisily.”; command is west movement key h after #kick.

The examined commit pins nethack-c/upstream to 16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4. Its src/dokick.c:1194-1241 evaluates the sink arm in order: Levitation, rn2(5) pipe vibration, black pudding, amorous demon, rn2(3) sink_backs_up, then kick_ouch. The recorded Klunk message proves this case takes the rn2(5) nonzero arm, which calls Soundeffect(se_klunk_pipe, 60), emits the Deaf-dependent line, exercises A_DEX positively, and returns ECMD_TIME.

Source ownership is confirmed at src/dokick.c:1465-1469: dokick() routes a non-door target to kick_nondoor(). At the examined commit js/dokick.js:865-869 throws for every sink before the first sink roll or side effect, so the cause is the missing source branch implementation rather than an RNG, display, or sink-helper defect.

src/fountain.c:805-825 defines sink_backs_up(), and js/fountain.js:1253-1281 already ports it. C calls it only in the final sink outcome at dokick.c:1235-1237; js/dokick.js has no call. Porting that helper alone would leave this case unchanged because the recorded C path returns from the earlier rn2(5) arm.

The prior investigation investigations/synthetic/v17/engrave-on-wished-undisturbed-grave-disturbs-it.json:168-169 identifies dokick.c:kick_nondoor() as the other caller of disturb_grave and documents a separate JS refusal in that same function. This confirms that a new task must account for the whole source function, as .agents/selection.md requires for partial C behavior; it does not explain the sink mismatch.

No source-owner ambiguity remains for this case. The whole-function port is broader than the recorded sink arm: js/dokick.js still refuses the secret-door, secret-corridor, fountain, grave-destruction, tree, and sink arms. Those are the function-wide scope to inspect during implementation; the current recording itself needs only the non-levitating rn2(5) pipe-vibration path.
